name: 3D Starling Murmuration
description: A real-time 3D flock of starlings from three local rules — the full multi-agent replay with phase-by-phase narration, two iterations + convergence, a basic interactive run, then the full Enhancement loop that adds topological neighbours, a predator, and density-wave shimmer.
spec: Build a real-time 3D murmuration — a flock of starlings — in a single self-contained HTML file using WebGL (Three.js). Each bird (boid) follows three local rules: separation (steer away from close neighbours), alignment (match the average heading of nearby neighbours), and cohesion (steer toward the local centre of mass). Render hundreds of birds as instanced cones flying at near-constant speed in a bounded volume. Provide live sliders for the three rule weights, perception radius, flock population and speed; plus camera orbit, selectable particle shapes and colour themes. The goal is a dense, sharply-defined, shape-shifting cloud that reads like a real starling murmuration at dusk. Target 60 fps with 1000+ birds and a graceful WebGL fallback.

## Design
1. Add colour themes (sunset / aurora / cyber) + particle shapes
2. Shimmer by banking (turn strength), not speed → density waves read clearly
3. Behaviour presets: Murmuration / Cyclone / Drifting Cloud

## Functionality
1. Topological neighbours (k=7) — cohesive flock that never fragments
2. Near-constant airspeed for silky, flowing motion
3. Autonomous predator → dramatic density waves & splitting

## Security
1. Clamp every slider param to a safe range on load
2. Graceful WebGL context-loss + fallback message
3. Bound predator & flee radius to the frustum

## Consolidated enhancement set
HIGH: 3 — topological neighbours (k=7), autonomous predator, near-constant speed
MEDIUM: 5 — palettes, particle shapes, presets, banking shimmer, FOV blind spot
LOW: 1 — camera auto-orbit easing

narration_chapters.title: Specification — your conversation with CodeForge
paragraphs: You're watching a replay of a real CodeForge session at 60× speed. No live LLM calls — every keystroke, audit and decision below actually happened, captured and played back so you can read at your own pace.
Every run starts here. The Specification is plain English: what to build, in what language, with what constraints. CodeForge turns it into a brief the whole agent team works from.
This demo asks for a real-time 3D murmuration — a flock of starlings — from three local rules: separation, alignment, cohesion. Hundreds of instanced birds in WebGL, live sliders, 60 fps.
Click the Spec node any time to re-read the full prompt. Press ▶ Continue to assemble the team and start coding.
narration_chapters.closing_paragraph: Spec received and parsed. Time to assemble the team and start coding.

narration_chapters.title: Coding round 1 — two coders in parallel
paragraphs: Two Coders pick up the spec and write independently — different models, different approaches. You'll see real streaming code scroll inside each Coder node as the LLM generates it.
Diverse vendors on purpose. Today: Coder 1 = claude-opus-4.5 (deep reasoning), Coder 2 = gpt-5.1-codex (fast, code-tuned). Divergence is a feature — the Finalizer picks the best later.
Both implement the same core: a Boid class, a spatial-hash grid for neighbour lookups, and the three steering rules accumulated into an acceleration each frame.
Self-test before submitting. After writing, each Coder runs its own code in a headless browser and screenshots it — so an obviously-broken build never reaches the Testers.
narration_chapters.closing_paragraph: Coding round 1 complete. Both Coders produced a running flock — but round-1 cuts always have rough edges the Testers will find.

narration_chapters.title: Testing round 1 — deep audit
paragraphs: Now the Testers take over. Each Tester reads every Coder's output and runs it — checking spec compliance, correctness, performance and code quality.
Different model families on purpose: claude-sonnet-4.5 + gemini-2.5-pro. Two perspectives catch more than one.
For a murmuration they look hard at the physics: does the flock stay together, or drift off-screen? Is the motion silky or jittery? Does it hold 60 fps at 1000 birds?
Severity tagging. Every issue becomes critical, serious, or minor — that ranking drives what the Coders fix next.
narration_chapters.closing_paragraph: Testing round 1 complete. Tester 1 flagged the flock dispersing off-screen (critical) and jittery speed (serious); Tester 2 added density and naming notes.

narration_chapters.title: Summarizer — the team lead
paragraphs: The Summarizer is the keystone of the loop. It reads ALL Tester audits, deduplicates, ranks by severity, and writes a single prioritised brief.
That brief becomes the next Coder iteration's input — so Coders fix the right things in the right order instead of guessing.
It doesn't touch code itself. Its job is to make sure the Coders know exactly what matters before they rewrite.
narration_chapters.closing_paragraph: Summary ready: Coder 1 must fix flock dispersion + speed jitter; Coder 2 sits clean this round.

narration_chapters.title: Iteration 2 — Coder 1 refines with feedback
paragraphs: Coder 1 had a critical + a serious issue. It now rewrites with the Summary in its prompt — adding frustum-fit bounds and angled reflection so the flock never leaves the frame.
Coder 2's round-1 version was clean, so it sits this iteration out — no need to burn tokens on a passing build.
Why audit context matters: without it, a single LLM tends to re-introduce the same bug. The loop is what makes it converge.
Watch the iteration badge in Coder 1's corner tick to 2.
narration_chapters.closing_paragraph: Round 2 coding complete. Coder 1 rebuilt its motion + bounds targeting the exact audit issues.

narration_chapters.title: Testing round 2 — did the fix work?
paragraphs: Testers run again with the previous Summary in their prompt — so they verify the specific fixes, not just re-scan blindly.
This independent re-verification is the part that's hard to replicate with a single LLM talking to itself.
If issues remain, Iteration 3 starts. If they're gone, the team converges early and saves the rest of the budget.
narration_chapters.closing_paragraph: Round 2 audit complete. Tester 1: 0 issues. Tester 2: one minor polish note. Converged.

narration_chapters.title: Summarizer round 2 — converged
paragraphs: All critical and serious issues are gone; one minor polish item remains. The Summarizer marks the run converged.
Budget was max 5 iterations — the team finished in 2 and banked the rest. Quality gates beat fixed loop counts.
narration_chapters.closing_paragraph: Converged in 2 of 5 allotted iterations. Handing both versions to the Finalizer.

narration_chapters.title: Finalizer — the judge
paragraphs: Two Coders, two versions. The Finalizer reads both — code, test scores and summaries — and picks the winner.
Plus a one-paragraph README explaining the choice, so the decision is auditable rather than a black box.
This is also where you'd plug in custom evaluation logic or a human Visual Review to override the model's pick.
narration_chapters.closing_paragraph: Winner: Coder 1's round-2 version — cohesive flock, smooth motion, cleaner control flow.

narration_chapters.title: First version is ready — try it
paragraphs: This is what a focused run of the basic spec gives you: a working 2D flock driven by the three rules with metric neighbours (everyone inside a fixed radius).
Click Run code to try it — full-screen, real boids, live sliders for separation / alignment / cohesion / population.
Notice what's missing vs. a finished piece: it's flat 2D, a single colour, no depth, no predator, and the flock can still loosen up. Honest first cut.
When you're ready: click Continue to bring in the Enhancement team.

narration_chapters.title: Enhancement — a second-pass team
paragraphs: Enhancement runs three specialists in parallel, each with a different lens — they get only the final code + original spec and propose targeted improvements.
Design — themes, particle shapes, and a shimmer that makes density waves read.
Functionality — the big physics upgrades: topological neighbours (k=7), near-constant airspeed, and an autonomous predator.
Security — clamp every parameter, handle WebGL context loss, bound the predator to the frame.
Then an Enh. Summarizer merges all three lists into one curated set you approve or reject item by item.
narration_chapters.closing_paragraph: Enhancement team briefed. Spinning up Design, Functionality and Security in parallel.

narration_chapters.title: Design / Functionality / Security — in parallel
paragraphs: All three run at once — the camera pans between them as each streams its findings.
Design (pink). Colour themes + particle shapes; shimmer by banking angle so the classic light/dark density waves appear; behaviour presets.
Functionality (cyan). Topological neighbours (k=7) like real starlings; constant airspeed; a roving hawk the flock evades — the heart of a real murmuration.
Security (red). Clamp slider ranges, graceful WebGL fallback, bound predator + flee radius.
Each writes ranked suggestions; once all three submit, the Enh. Summarizer consolidates.
narration_chapters.closing_paragraph: All three submitted: Design 3, Functionality 3, Security 3. Merging next.

narration_chapters.title: Enh. Summarizer — merge into one curated list
paragraphs: Reads all three specialist lists, deduplicates, and ranks into one set: HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW.
You're the editor — agents propose, you decide. In the real product each item has an Apply / Reject toggle.
Apply spawns a NEW session that continues from your final code with the curated improvements folded into the spec.
narration_chapters.closing_paragraph: Consolidated: 3 HIGH (topological, predator, constant speed), 5 MEDIUM, 1 LOW.

narration_chapters.title: Enhanced rerun — full cycle, faster
paragraphs: Same Coders, but now their spec includes the curated improvements. They write topological neighbours, the predator and constant-speed motion straight in.
In reality this is another full multi-iteration cycle; the demo compresses it. Watch the same nodes light up: Coders → Testers → Finalizer.
The result is the dense, sharply-defined, shape-shifting cloud a real murmuration makes — density waves and all.
narration_chapters.closing_paragraph: Enhanced rerun finished. The richer version converged in one extra iteration.

narration_chapters.title: Enhanced final version — try it & build your own
paragraphs: After Enhancement the same agents produced a much richer version: full 3D, topological neighbours (k=7), an autonomous predator carving density waves, palettes, presets and banking shimmer.
Click Run enhanced code to interact with the full version — orbit the camera, toggle the predator, switch to metric neighbours and watch the flock loosen.
When you're ready to make your own: Try it yourself. CodeForge will run this exact pipeline live on whatever you ask for.

Interactive Swarm Engine

Boids & Murmuration

Three local rules · one flock behavior. No one has an overall plan. Each particle looks only at its nearest neighbors and obeys three simple rules. From this a living, fluid swarm emerges by itself — like a flock of starlings at sunset.

Core Local Rules

Steer away to avoid crowding or colliding with close neighbors.
Steer toward the average center of mass of local neighbors.
Steer towards the average heading velocity of nearby neighbors.
The view distance within which neighbors are analyzed.
Topological Neighbors (k=7)
Each bird tracks its 7 nearest neighbors — like real starlings — instead of everyone in range. Keeps the flock cohesive and sharply defined (the single biggest realism lever).
Predator (Hawk)
A roving hawk the flock continuously evades — produces the dramatic density waves, splitting and re-forming of a true murmuration.
Light-independent emissive glow applied directly in the shader.
Pushes the emissive color toward pure highlights and deep shadows before the brightness gain is applied.
Reflect at Boundaries
When on, the swarm senses the screen walls early: it slows and curves back inward at an angle before reaching the edge, and any boid that still touches a wall is reflected (angle of incidence equals angle of reflection) — never crossing the bounds.
Adaptive Quality
Automatically lowers resolution then population if the frame rate drops, and restores resolution when it recovers.
